source.title: Spectral Superposition: A Theory of Feature Geometry
source.authors: G. Ivanov; N. Oozeer; Shivam Raval; Tasana Pejovic; S. Upadhyay; Amir Abdullah

record.file_problem: The supplied extraction ends after Figure 39 in Appendix I; whether more source text exists is not stated. Equations and some figures also have extraction or formatting artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes the canonical toy model with a new spectral framework and reports a parameter sweep, theoretical results, and geometric classifications. It is not an explicit replication using the original study's measures.
record.gate_note: The paper's own toy-model sweep and its stated theoretical results are included. Cited results about LLMs, SAEs, refusal features, and prior toy-model geometries are not rows. The appendix's non-uniform-sparsity section contains figure placeholders but no extractable reported outcome.
record.test_reason: The study trains the canonical TMS toy model across a 3,200-run sweep (n=1024, m in [16,512], 50 sparsity levels). It reports capacity use and spectral localization of features, and proves that capacity saturation forces tight-frame cluster geometry. This bears on V1 using a different (spectral) method. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors also claim the theory gives a complete description of the TMS geometries and argue that weight-induced operators, not individual feature vectors, are the right units for studying superposition. They note that localization in real models is suggested by HT-SR but not measured.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the toy-model reconstruction setup and weighted MSE described as being as in the original, but conducts a larger parameter sweep and analyzes spectral measures and feature geometry rather than relying on the original study's method and measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported localization and capacity slack vary with sparsity: higher sparsity is associated with more diffuse feature spectral mass and a slight departure from capacity saturation.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors argue that weight-induced operators (frame-operator eigenspaces), rather than individual feature vectors, are the appropriate units for analysing superposition. They illustrate this with a stylized rock-paper-scissors/heads-tails example of structural interference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature geometry (shared eigenspaces, symmetry) carries information that sparse per-feature decompositions discard.

record.problems: The empirical figures are described without extractable numerical values for individual settings. The sweep uses uniform feature importance, and no control condition is reported. The empirical results concern toy models; the paper does not measure LLM features. Some appendix figures appear only as placeholders in the supplied extraction.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise eligible own results were omitted. Cited findings about LLMs, SAEs, refusal, and prior toy-model geometries were excluded because they are not results of this study.

untested.parts: The sparsity-dependent transition (onset of superposition versus sparsity) is not reported per sparsity level. Feature importance is held uniform, so importance-dependent geometry is not tested. Per-setting numerical values are not extractable.
Not tested: importance is uniform and there is no neuron-level polysemanticity analysis.
Not tested; incidental polysemanticity is only cited (Lecomte et al.).
Not tested; no LLM activations or SAE recovery.
Not tested; SAEs are critiqued only conceptually.
Not tested; there is no comparison of intrinsically 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Non-uniform sparsity runs: the text says the same projective linearity is observed, but the figures are placeholders with no values.
Leverage-weighted tail mass of high-slack (delocalized, 'dark matter') features stays small across sparsity. Includes the well-behaved vs dark-matter spectral entropy distributions.
missing.locator: Appendix D (empirical interpretation), Appendix I Figure 17

missing.what: A theoretical result that tight-frame configurations under uniform sparsity are spectral fixed points of the gradient flow, offered as an explanation of the stable geometries.

record.verdict_notes: Most rows are conditional theorems rather than measurements; only R1 and R2 are empirical, and no numerical values are extractable for them. The text gives plot descriptions only. Many appendix figures are placeholders.

versions.untested_parts: The sweep holds feature importance uniform. It does not establish a sparsity-dependent transition threshold or give numerical outcomes for individual sparsity levels.
The paper tests capacity use in toy models with uniform importance, but not whether features of differing importance receive dedicated dimensions while less important features share.
The paper mentions incidental polysemanticity from prior work but does not test whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
No LLM activations, neuron-feature spread, or SAE recovery is measured.
The paper discusses feature extraction methods but does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical.

The paper formalizes features as weight columns and tests their spectral localization, but does not compare semantic features that are intrinsically one-dimensional with intrinsically multidimensional features.

rows.subject: toy models of superposition
rows.operation_detail: Measured the sum of feature fractional dimensionalities across a sweep of 3,200 training runs.
rows.measure: Sum of individual feature fractional dimensionalities, Σi Di, compared with hidden dimension m
rows.value: Approximately all hidden-dimension capacity is used (Σi Di ≈ m); the paper reports a slight deviation in the high-sparsity regime.
rows.note: The text describes near-saturation across runs and says higher sparsity accounts for a slight deviation; it gives no numerical values for the plotted results.
rows.check: Σ Di ≈ m across runs, with only slight high-sparsity deviation, is near-full capacity use by features in superposition, so the state is observed, not partial. The V2 link is removed: importance is uniform, no neurons are examined, and no dedicated-vs-shared allocation by importance is tested. No numeric values are readable from Figure 5.

rows.subject: toy models of superposition
rows.size_stated: n = 1024 features; 3,276,800 total features analyzed across 3,200 runs
rows.operation_detail: Measured cluster spectral localization using mean maximum spectral mass and compared it with the linear-fit R².
rows.measure: Mean maximum spectral mass per cluster; relationship with the R² of the projective-linearity fit
rows.value: Lower sparsity is associated with tighter configurations and stronger localization; higher sparsity is associated with more diffuse spectral mass, including a few delocalized features.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 6 describes error bars as absolute error |kλ − 1|; numeric error values not stated.
rows.note: The paper describes the trend but does not state plotted numerical values or report separate values for individual sparsity levels.
rows.check: Localization (regular eigenspace geometry) is strong at low sparsity. At high sparsity spectral mass is more diffuse and a few features delocalize. The V6 link is removed: features are weight columns by construction, and the row does not compare 1-D with multi-dimensional features. No plotted numbers are extractable.

rows.subject: toy models of superposition
rows.size_stated: n features in m dimensions; no specific size for the theorem
rows.operation_detail: Proved spectral localization conditional on saturation of the fractional-dimensionality capacity bound.
rows.value: For every feature i, the spectral measure is a single Dirac mass at a positive eigenvalue; equivalently, FWi = λkWi.
rows.note: This is a conditional theorem, not an empirical finding that every trained model achieves exact saturation.
rows.check: This is a conditional theorem (saturation implies Dirac spectral measure), not an empirical measurement; it is kept as the study's own theoretical result. The V6 link is removed for the same reason as R2.

rows.subject: toy models of superposition
rows.size_stated: n features in m dimensions; no specific size for the theorem
rows.operation_detail: Derived the feature-cluster geometry from spectral localization.

conditions.value: Spectral localization holds for all features

rows.value: Features sharing an eigenvalue form a tight frame in their span; distinct-eigenvalue feature spans are orthogonal.
rows.note: The theorem permits a cluster span to have dimension greater than one; it does not require a cluster to be a collection of mutually orthogonal vectors.
rows.check: This is a theorem conditional on localization: clusters are tight frames and spans for distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal. The V6 link is removed; multi-dimensional cluster spans are groups of 1-D features, not multi-dimensional features in V6's sense.

rows.subject: toy models of superposition
rows.size_stated: cluster size and span dimension vary; no specific size for the theorem
rows.operation_detail: Gave a spectral criterion for identifying cluster geometry using association schemes.

conditions.value: Spectral localization and the tight-frame result hold

rows.measure: Alignment of local Gram-matrix eigenspaces with association-scheme strata
rows.value: A cluster geometry is an instance of an association scheme if and only if the local Gram-matrix eigenspaces align with the scheme's canonical strata; the paper also gives a simplex-identification corollary.
rows.locator: Section 4, Theorem 4 and Corollary 5; Appendix C
rows.note: The paper says this characterizes geometries in the toy-model setting, including previously described simplices, polygons, and a square antiprism; those prior observations are not new experimental rows.
rows.check: This is a theorem and corollary giving a spectral classification criterion. Its application to simplices, polygons and the antiprism re-describes geometries reported in the original, not new observations. The V6 link is removed.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4, Theorem 4 and Corollary 5; Appendix C, corresponding statements and proofs.
